newsitem.title: USA: NYC MAC refunding saves $52 mln -- Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: NYC MAC refunding saves $52 mln -- Morgan Stanley.

text.p: Morgan Stanley & Co on Thursday said a $680 million refunding by the Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York saved approximately $52 million on a present value basis.
Rocky Query, a principal with Morgan Stanley, told a MAC board meeting that the savings worked out to about 7.9 percent of the refunded bonds.

Noting the market's sharp volatility on Wednesday, he attributed the sale's success to about $100 million of retail orders that were received, along with $400 million institutional priority orders, as well as strong support from the underwriters.
Corporations and trust funds focused their interest in the short-end of the offering, while longer term maturities drew property and casualty insurers and intermediate mutual funds, Query said.
MAC officials complimented the underwriting group's handling of the issue, noting that they were able to increase the size of the deal despite a falling market.

"This is a case where the underwriters, particularly Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs really stepped up. Lesser mortals might have asked for a repricing to make the deal more palatable and they did not," Quentin Specter, executive director at MAC, said.
The Morgan Stanley official said the refunding achieved the lowest financing cost for MAC since 1993.
